title: ValidateJWTSVID ignores the trust bundle and verifies only against the local ephemeral key
description:
NOT a verification bypass - it is fail-closed - but the validation path is wrong and the code comment misdescribes it.

persona-grpc/src/service.rs:219-221:
    // Get the local trust bundle public key for verification.
    let pub_key_der = self.signer.public_key_der();
    let decoding_key = DecodingKey::from_ec_der(pub_key_der);
self.bundles (the TrustBundleStore, service.rs:18) is never consulted. The only accepted issuer is this processs own ephemeral keypair.

CONSEQUENCE:
1. Federation does not work. Any SVID from a peer trust domain present in the bundle store is rejected with "JWT validation failed", even though the whole point of TrustBundleStore is to hold those authorities. Callers get a signature error rather than a trust error, which will send integrators down the wrong path.
2. Every SVID is rejected after a personad restart, because the CA key is ephemeral (persona-core/src/signer.rs:53-54, personad/src/main.rs:31) and the new process cannot verify tokens the old one signed. No error distinguishes "key rotated" from "forged".
3. No trust-domain binding is checked. The verified tokens spiffe_id claim is read at service.rs:230-235 and returned, but nothing asserts that its trust domain corresponds to the bundle/key that verified it. Once more than one key is in play, a key valid for trust domain A will happily validate an ID claiming trust domain B.

Positives, so they are not re-reviewed: Validation::new(Algorithm::ES256) (service.rs:223) pins the algorithm, so jsonwebtoken 9 rejects alg:none and HS256 header substitution; set_audience (service.rs:224) with validate_aud on by default; validate_exp on by default. The algorithm-confusion class is genuinely closed here.

Fix direction: select the verification key from self.bundles by the tokens trust domain (JWKS by kid), and assert the resulting trust domain matches the bundle that verified it.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.82 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
